clue.text: Adoring hip-hop singer in pieces without awful noise

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled letters sit around the noise
broken into pieces, so the letters of hip-hop singer are smashed up and reassembled

parts.note: a row is a loud din or racket

explanation.surface: A fan worships a rapper who is falling apart, apparently without making much of a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: the anagram of HIPHOPSINGER ('in pieces') goes round ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe idolising someone; adoring a star is the same as treating them as an idol.

clue.text: Bobby Charlton's header, running fast after cut back by reserve

indicators.note: the cut-back-and-reserve part comes before the rest in the answer
sending the word for a cut back means writing it from right to left

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
ice is coolness of manner, reserve
on, as a machine is running

explanation.surface: A football report: Bobby Charlton's header and a fast run after being held back by a reserve player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobby Charlton' reads as the footballer, but Bobby is the definition, a British nickname for a police officer after Sir Robert Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby is British slang for a police officer, from Robert Peel, founder of the Metropolitan force.

clue.text: Disapproval for Mister Barking's promotional activity

parts.note: boo is a cry of disapproval
the S of the possessive is part of the fodder

indicators.note: barking mad, crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A crowd jeers a man nicknamed Mister Barking for his relentless self-promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' is British slang for mad and signals an anagram of MISTER, giving TERISM; the S of the possessive sits before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Boosterism is enthusiastic promotion of a town, cause or product, i.e. promotional activity.

clue.text: One with no degree of theatre work in Tudor plays

indicators.note: the work is placed inside the rearranged letters
the letters of Tudor play about, i.e. move around

parts.note: op, short for opus, a work, such as one for the stage

explanation.surface: Someone without a degree performs in a Tudor drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' signals an anagram of TUDOR (DROUT), with OP inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A dropout leaves college before graduating, so never earns a qualification.

clue.text: Paper bags quietly turned around

indicators.note: to bag is to take hold of, so the paper holds the quiet letter

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
p, piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A newspaper quietly bags a story and then does a U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spun has rotated, so it has turned around.

clue.text: Where people are both in and out of capital?

definitions.text: Where people are both in and out of capital?

parts.words: Where people are both in and out of capital?
parts.note: commuters live outside the capital city yet work in the City and deal in money capital

explanation.surface: A riddle about people who are simultaneously inside and outside the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital is both London, which these people leave each evening, and money, which they handle all day.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the affluent commuter belt around London where City financiers live.

clue.text: Moralising work of Corbyn is trashed with gusto

indicators.note: wrecked, so the letters of the fodder are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A preachy book by Jeremy Corbyn is enthusiastically slated by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: Baden-Powell's 1908 handbook for the Boy Scouts gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Baden-Powell's book is full of earnest instruction on character and conduct for youngsters.

clue.text: Time to attack endlessly unfair work conditions

indicators.note: the last letter is removed from the phrase

parts.note: zero hours contracts guarantee no work, widely seen as unfair

explanation.surface: Workers on unfair contracts decide it is time to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: Zero-hours contracts, common in Britain, promise no fixed hours; dropping the final S leaves the military term.
explanation.definitionFit: The scheduled moment when a military operation begins is the time to strike.

clue.text: Express's quiet about Conservative power grab

parts.note: to put something is to express it in words

indicators.note: the hush goes around the Conservative

explanation.surface: The Daily Express keeps quiet about a Tory power grab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like the newspaper but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup or violent seizure of government is a grab for power.

clue.text: They reward theatrics from the likes of Blair?

definitions.meaning: the Tony Awards honour Broadway theatre
people called Tony, such as Tony Blair

explanation.surface: Prizes for histrionics from politicians such as Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tony Awards are Broadway's prizes, and Tony Blair is a former British prime minister.

clue.text: In charge in any pub, moving stock up frantically

indicators.note: the letters of any pub, with the abbreviation for in charge, move about into a new order

explanation.surface: The person in charge of any pub moves stock frantically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' signals an anagram of IC plus ANY PUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic buying is hoarding goods in fear of shortages.

clue.text: Put up with someone hard to put up with

definitions.text: someone hard to put up with

explanation.surface: Tolerated someone intolerable.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of bear means tolerated; a tedious person is also so called.

clue.text: One in the balance on horse almost balances

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another follows it
the last letter is left off

parts.note: an equid is any member of the horse family

indicators.note: the one goes inside the balance

parts.note: Libra, the zodiac sign of the scales

explanation.surface: Someone balancing on a horse, almost.
explanation.definitionFit: Equilibria are states of balance, plural like balances.

clue.text: Appear with the greatest film doubles

parts.note: Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest
Kes, Ken Loach's 1969 film about a boy and his kestrel

explanation.surface: Body doubles appear alongside the greatest film stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Kes is a classic British film; Ali's nickname was The Greatest.
explanation.definitionFit: People who closely resemble someone are their doubles.

clue.text: Effortless adoption thus returned second sibling

indicators.note: turned back, so the letters run right to left

explanation.surface: An adoption story: the returned second sibling was taken in easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adoption' suggests a family, but it means picking up ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbing knowledge gradually and unconsciously is figuratively called this.

clue.text: Hygiene issue not even in town

explanation.surface: A hygiene problem that is patchy across town.
explanation.definitionFit: A municipal division or town with its own corporation.

clue.text: Jack ejected from meeting for insincere emotion

parts.note: a junction is a meeting of roads

explanation.definitionFit: Unction is affected, oily earnestness or gushing manner.

clue.text: Condition of lush sauces by Arab American

explanation.surface: A lush condition brought about by sauces from an Arab American.
explanation.definitionFit: Craving for alcohol is the affliction of a heavy drinker.

clue.text: Desire heterosexual embraces

indicators.note: the word holds the answer inside it

explanation.surface: Heterosexual passion in a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love and the term for sexual longing.

clue.text: Stylish and posh, favourite clothing brand

indicators.note: dressing, so the favourite goes round the brand

explanation.surface: A stylish posh clothing brand that is a favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing brand' looks like a fashion label, but clothing is a container indicator; U is the classic abbreviation for upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Upscale goods aimed at wealthy buyers are smart and stylish.

clue.text: Strip and remove shell of jet plane

parts.note: a football kit is a strip

indicators.note: the outer letters are stripped away

explanation.surface: Stripping down a jet plane.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip is British for a team's football kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Kite is old RAF slang for an aircraft.

clue.text: Setter and setter drinking drink and drink

explanation.surface: Two setters drinking round after round.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe means to consume liquor.

clue.text: Deer's back, lassoed by worker's chain

indicators.note: caught in a loop, put inside
the word for deer runs backwards

explanation.surface: A deer's back was roped by a worker's chain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental chain worn around the ankle.

clue.text: Covers no more songs

explanation.surface: No more songs: cover versions.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlays are layers placed on top, i.e. covers.
